prompt:
Extract the one contact record from the user's note. Use only its label–value lines, which may appear in any order with label variants and colon, equals or tab separators. Ignore all surrounding text and signatures. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country; every value is a string or JSON null. No other text.

Trim each value and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent or empty values and the case-insensitive placeholders -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD are null. Do not infer missing values except for country as specified below.

Route any value containing @ to email. Route any value consisting only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / with at least seven digits after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension to phone, regardless of label. Extensions include ext. followed by digits, ext followed by digits, x plus digits, # plus digits, and extension followed by digits. Use the name and company labels for those fields, except swap their values if the name value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company value does not. Use only the country line for an explicit country.

Name: split at the first comma and move the right side before the left; remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof, case-insensitively with or without a dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics without transliteration; comparison is NFC-normalised.
Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
Email: unwrap surrounding angle brackets and strip mailto: so neither remains; lowercase the address.
Country: convert the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases, all case-insensitively: UK or Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA or U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.
Phone: after removing tel: and the extension, detect international format by a leading + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. For international phones, turn 00 into +, remove (0), strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and keep the written calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. For national phones, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the explicit country's calling code; without a country, return null. Phone strings are E.164: + followed by calling-code and national-significant-number digits only.

If the country line is absent, empty or a placeholder and the phone is international, fill country from the calling code only if it uniquely identifies a country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, give null. This is the sole exception to missing values staying null. Never use email domains, company suffixes or surrounding notes to infer other fields.
